transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. Can you tell me what brings you in today?

I came in because things at work kind of swung really hard. I was launching plant redesign projects nonstop, calling suppliers after hours, rewriting the shift plan by myself… and then all of a sudden I couldn’t keep up with the plans I’d put in motion. It got out of hand, and I need help figuring out what’s going on.
Have you noticed a period of time where you felt unusually energized, needed less sleep, or were more productive than usual — even before things started to feel overwhelming?

Yes. For a while I had this extra energy that didn’t feel normal for me. I’d be unpacking after midnight, reorganizing the apartment, answering work emails, and even after all that I’d still feel like I should go back to the plant to check one more thing.
During that time when you had all that extra energy, did you also feel unusually high, euphoric, or maybe more irritable than usual?

Yes. At the start of that assignment I felt almost... electrically upbeat, like everything I was thinking made perfect sense and needed to happen right away. But it also turned into irritability. If someone questioned my ideas, I felt like they were just slowing down something that was obviously important.
During that time when you felt so energized and upbeat, did you find that you needed a lot less sleep than usual?

Yes. I was sleeping maybe two or three hours a night, and somehow I’d still show up at the plant feeling sharp and charged. At the time it almost felt like sleep was optional, or like it was kind of inefficient.
How long did you feel that way — the upbeat, energized, and irritable part — before it started to feel overwhelming or you couldn’t keep up?

It’s been about three weeks, since I moved into the temporary apartment. That’s when it really shifted into overdrive. And then it started swinging into where I could barely function and couldn’t keep up.
After that initial period of high energy and irritability, did you continue to feel consistently elevated or irritable, or did your mood start to change and swing in another direction?

It definitely started to change. Lately I wake up in the temporary apartment with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day is already ruined before I even drive to the plant. It doesn’t feel elevated anymore.
Have you felt down or hopeless nearly every day, or lost interest in activities you usually enjoy, for most of the day — and has this lasted for at least two weeks?

Yes. Lately I’ve been waking up in the temporary apartment with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day is already ruined before I even get to work. It’s been most days, and it stays with me a lot of the day.
Have you noticed a loss of pleasure in things you usually enjoy, or felt fatigued or worthless nearly every day during this low mood?

I’m not really sure. I know I’ve been low most days, but I haven’t really tracked whether it’s specifically a loss of pleasure or feeling worthless. Fatigue… maybe, but I can’t say it’s been nearly every day for sure.

Can you describe if there was a time when your mood was clearly different from your usual self — like feeling unusually high, overly confident, or irritable to the point where people around you noticed a change?

Yes. At the beginning of this assignment, I felt really different from my normal self. I was almost electrically upbeat, like everything was clear and I had all this momentum. Then it shifted into this weird irritability — if anyone questioned my ideas, I felt like they were just slowing down something obvious and important.
During this low mood phase, did you feel down or irritable most of the day, nearly every day, or was it more on and off?

It’s been more like most of the day, most days. I wake up in that temporary apartment with this heavy, hollow feeling, like the day is already ruined before I even drive to the plant, and it tends to stay with me.
